title: A circuit breaker with a half-open probe

task.text: Stop calling a dependency that keeps failing, then probe it to see if it recovered.

Implement `CircuitBreaker(int threshold, long openMs, LongSupplier clock)` with `State state()` and `<T> T call(Supplier<T> op, Supplier<T> fallback)`. `State` is given. Time comes only from `clock` (ms).

items: **CLOSED:** run `op`. A `RuntimeException` counts as a failure and returns `fallback.get()`. A success resets the count of consecutive failures.
`threshold` consecutive failures make it **OPEN**: `op` is not called, callers get `fallback.get()`.
Once `openMs` have passed, one caller becomes the probe and the state is **HALF_OPEN**; everyone else still gets the fallback.
A successful probe closes the breaker; a failed probe reopens it and restarts the cool-down.
Never hold a lock while `op` runs.

checks.title: A closed breaker passes calls through
Open rejects without calling the operation
After the cool-down one call probes
A failed probe reopens and restarts the timer
Other callers are rejected during the probe
Racing callers cause exactly one probe
A slow call does not hold a lock
Only the injected clock is used

hints.text: Three states and two counters: consecutive failures, and when it opened. The hard part is the transition OPEN to HALF_OPEN: exactly one caller may take it.

Split `call` into `permit()` and `record(boolean ok)`, both `synchronized`, with `op.get()` between them, outside the lock. `permit()` flips OPEN to HALF_OPEN and returns true for that one caller only.
